subject: Annual School Handbook Review Process Policy
overview: The subcommittee drafted and approved a new policy, CHCA-B, establishing a four-phase timeline and procedure for the annual review and approval of school handbooks. The proposed process requires the administration and school councils to provide detailed memoranda of substantive changes to facilitate informed School Committee oversight.

items.title: Establishment of Handbook Review Norms
items.summary: The subcommittee convened to establish a formal process for the annual school handbook review as mandated by a previous resolution.

items.title: Historical Context and Policy Gaps
items.summary: Chair Ruseau discussed the legal requirement for annual approval and the current lack of consistency in content and formatting across district schools.

items.title: Phase 1: Initiation of Update Process
items.summary: The body reviewed the first phase of the draft policy, which requires the Superintendent to update handbook drafts with mandatory legal and policy changes between August and September.

items.title: Phase 2: School Council Recommendations
items.summary: The policy draft directs school councils to recommend additional updates and submit them to the Superintendent alongside a memorandum of substantive changes.

items.title: Phase 3: School Committee Review Timeline
items.summary: Members discussed a phase for committee review to occur between February and April to ensure completion before the end-of-year event season begins in May.

items.title: Approval and Amendment Procedures
items.summary: The subcommittee clarified that handbooks should be approved in whole, though specific sections may be referred to subcommittees if discrepancies arise.

items.title: District-Wide Consistency Review
items.summary: The body added a requirement for the Superintendent to review handbooks for consistency across schools regarding items like homework and recess protocols.

items.title: Onboarding and Efficiency Concerns
items.summary: Members discussed the difficulty of onboarding new members to the review process and the necessity of using concise memoranda to handle the high volume of documentation.

items.title: Recommendation of Policy CHCA-B
items.summary: Approved a motion to report Policy CHCA-B to the full School Committee with a recommendation for adoption.
